sections.label: Formation of GovTech
sections.summary: This Bill provides for the formation of the Government Technology Agency, or GovTech, focused on ICT and related engineering.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The other part of this restructuring process is the formation of a dedicated organisation focused on info-communications technology (ICT) and related engineering, called the Government Technology Agency, or GovTech for short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This Bill provides for the formation of GovTech.

sections.label: Government IT management and satisfaction
sections.summary: It manages IT departments of about two-thirds of Government agencies, and nine in 10 Singaporeans are satisfied with e-services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, it directly manages the IT departments of about two-thirds of all Government agencies and handles other critical systems for the rest of the public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Nine out of 10 Singaporeans are satisfied with the overall quality of Government e-services, and Singapore is regularly ranked amongst the best digital governments in the world.

sections.label: Digital services for citizens
sections.summary: It will spur the public sector to design responsive digital services, such as MyInfo and the Business Grants Portal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: It will also spur the public sector to design digital services that are responsive to citizens' needs and provide a better experience when interacting with the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We can look forward to more services, such as the recently launched MyInfo, which removes the need for citizens to repeatedly provide the same personal data when transacting with different Government agencies, or the Business Grants Portal which allows small and medium enterprises (SMEs) a one-stop platform to look for relevant financial assistance.

sections.label: GovTech functions and powers
sections.summary: Part 2 spells out GovTech's functions and powers, including ensuring security and reliability of ICT systems and promoting standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Part 2 also spells out GovTech's functions and powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These include new functions which were not contained in the IDA Act but which will be essential for GovTech's expanded role, such as to ensure the security and reliability of ICT and related engineering systems and services in the public sector, as well as to promote competencies and professional standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Part 7 of the Bill empowers GovTech with the statutory mandate and powers to ensure the security and reliability of ICT systems and services, and to level up technology standards across the public sector.

sections.label: Extending governance beyond public sector
sections.summary: Part 8 empowers GovTech to extend its governance measures and standards to non-Government bodies providing essential public sector-related functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Part 8 empowers GovTech to extend its governance measures and standards beyond the public sector to non-Government bodies providing essential public sector-related functions.

sections.label: GovTech role in Smart Nation
sections.summary: GovTech will play a critical role in the Government's digital transformation, replacing the GCIO wing of the current IDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: GovTech will play a critical role in the digital transformation of the Government, which is a key plank in our Smart Nation vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new GovTech aims to harness and deploy ICT services that benefit Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Replacing the Government Chief Information Office (GCIO) wing of the current IDA, it will build on its traditional strength of enterprise IT to take on new functions, as the Minister described earlier on, the digital transformation of the public sector, growing deep technical capabilities, seeing to governance and standards, looking into cybersecurity and managing the Smart Nation platform, solutions and applications.

sections.label: GovTech Smart Nation platform data
sections.summary: GovTech will set up the Smart Nation platform, which collects data for policy-makers in fields including urban planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: GovTech will aid this effort also by setting up the Smart Nation platform, which will collect data that can then be analysed by policy-makers in various fields, including urban planning.

sections.label: GovTech synergies with other agencies
sections.summary: A question asks how GovTech will create synergies with SNPO, DSTA and CSA and minimise duplication of work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Page: 136 As GovTech develops expertise in a broad range of technology areas, including cybersecurity, how will it aim to create synergies with other agencies, such as the Smart Nation Programme Office (SNPO), Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) and Cyber Security Agency (CSA), and minimise duplication of work and harness the synergies?

sections.label: GovTech established for Smart Nation
sections.summary: GovTech was established to enhance Singapore's Smart Nation effort and lead the public sector in applying technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: GovTech was established to enhance Singapore's effort to fulfil its Smart Nation aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is hoped that this new agency will achieve the objective of leading the public sector and the Government in terms of improving the application of technology in order to provide a more effective service to the people and corporate organisations.

sections.label: GovTech functions, powers and procurement
sections.summary: GovTech will be the Government's main technology agency, with powers to procure ICT goods and issue directives, codes and standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With all these functions, GovTech will be the Government's main agency in the usage of technology and there is room for it to operate outside the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Just like the infocomm media sector, GovTech will also require investments and planning to develop expertise and manpower capabilities in order to successfully develop those sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new GovTech will and I quote, from the Bill, "undertake the procurement of ICT and related engineering goods for the public sector…" It will have powers and I quote, "to issue directives, codes, standards and guidelines for the public sector in relation to the architecture or use of ICT or related engineering systems or services in the public sector." The new agency recalls one of the core functions of the National Computer Board, formed in 1981, which was to implement the computerisation of the Civil Service.

sections.label: GovTech data and privacy impact assessments
sections.summary: A question asks whether GovTech will conduct and encourage other public sector agencies to conduct privacy impact assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new GovTech will have access to a great deal of personal and corporate data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a best practice, will GovTech conduct and encourage other public sector agencies to conduct privacy impact assessments?

sections.label: CSA located in PMO
sections.summary: A question asks why the Cyber Security Agency, formed in April 2015, is located within the Prime Minister's Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I would like to ask why the Cyber Security Agency (CSA), formed in April 2015, is located within the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

sections.label: NETS electronic payments interoperability
sections.summary: NETS launched in 1985 but has not become more inter-operable, being limited to one associated bank and not interoperable with international card schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For instance, our current landscape for electronic payments seems to be playing catch-up to developments in some other major cities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We had started out quite strongly when the Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) was launched in 1985 but NETS has not evolved to be more inter-operable, being only available to consumers of one of the associated banks in Singapore and not interoperable with international card schemes.

sections.label: Digital payment system and GovTech priorities
sections.summary: An efficient digital payment system with common infrastructure, central addressing and unified point-of-sale is suggested as a GovTech priority, along with harnessing resources and underserved communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The development of an efficient digital payment system with common infrastructure at the base level, a central addressing system where citizens can transact with one another safely and effectively and a unified point-of-sale solution for consumers is probably the way to go.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Such an overhaul will require a multi-agency effort and I would like to suggest that this be one of the key priorities for GovTech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The second area of focus I would like to suggest to GovTech to look at is to use technology and solutions to better harness resources in the society and also unleash the potential in traditionally underserved or special needs communities in Singapore.

sections.label: Cyberattacks in 2015
sections.summary: A cited source reported over a thousand successful cyberattacks in 2015, leaking 300 million records and almost $1 billion in stolen money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on a source cited by Tech Insider, there were more than a thousand successful cyberattacks in 2015 that led to a leak of 300 million records and almost $1 billion in stolen money.

sections.label: Singpass security breach risk
sections.summary: With over 3.3 million Singpass users, a security breach would cripple e-services and harm personal data, so GovTech coordinates cybersecurity with CSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With more than 3.3 million Singpass users transacting with the Government, it is not hard to imagine how a breach in Singpass security, for example, would cripple our e-services system and would have serious repercussions on the personal data of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The danger is very real and it is not one that we can afford to take lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am thus particularly glad that one of the key roles of GovTech is to coordinate the Government's cybersecurity jointly with CSA.

sections.label: GovTech working with private corporations
sections.summary: The Minister said GovTech would work closely with private corporations of public interest to enhance services delivered to public consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although primarily focusing on public agencies, I was heartened to hear the Minister say earlier that GovTech would also work closely with private corporations of public interest to enhance the quality of services that these entities deliver to public consumers.

sections.label: Citizen co-creation of digital services
sections.summary: Minister Yaacob shared this encourages citizens to co-create public digital services, in line with Smart Nation participation from non-government stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Yaacob shared that this will encourage citizens to participate in the co-creation of public digital services, in line with our Smart Nation initiative to solicit participation from non-government stakeholders to contribute innovative ideas and solutions.

sections.label: Thanks for whole-of-Government approach
sections.summary: The speaker thanks the Minister for a new whole-of-Government approach to cut administrative burdens in Government transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I thank the Minister for the new whole-of-Government approach to cut down on administrative burdens in Government transactions.

sections.label: Question on new agency committees
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister if setting up new agencies like GovTech and IMDA can be accompanied by committees with more people from diverse backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Minister if the setting up of the new agencies, such as GovTech and also previously, IMDA, can be accompanied with committees comprising more people on the ground, from more diverse backgrounds.

sections.label: Unified terminals and mobile addressing
sections.summary: Initiatives include unified point-of-sale terminals and a central mobile addressing system for near-instant interbank transfers, and IDA is exploring a common secure mobile digital identity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Initiatives that are being developed include unified point-of-sale terminals and a central mobile addressing system that allows payers to make near-instant interbank fund transfers as long as they know the payee's mobile number.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: IDA is also exploring the possibility of a common and secure mobile digital identity to enable convenient and secure digital transactions.

sections.label: GovTech and CSA cybersecurity centre
sections.summary: GovTech and CSA will jointly set up a capability centre in cybersecurity to deepen the Government's capabilities in protecting against cyber threats.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As GovTech and CSA both require cybersecurity expertise, they will jointly set up a capability centre in cybersecurity to deepen the Government's capabilities in protecting against cyber threats.

sections.label: Accredited companies and awarded projects
sections.summary: 15 companies have been accredited, and 35 projects have been awarded to startups and SMEs accredited by IDA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, we have accredited 15 companies, and 35 projects have been awarded to startups and SMEs accredited by IDA.

sections.label: ICT tenders and data protection rules
sections.summary: The majority of ICT tenders are awarded to SMEs, and the public sector has robust data protection rules similar to those under the PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In response to Mr Leon Perera's question, the majority of the ICT tenders are awarded to our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: On Mr Leon Perera's point about privacy impact assessment, the public sector has in place a robust set of data protection rules, which are similar to those under the PDPA.
